excluded_from_promotion.csql.err: CUBRID client-side connect log. Inspected before exclusion: it contains only 'Program csql ... connected' NOTIFICATION lines and boot_cl.c:875 CODE=-971 notifications, i.e. one entry per client connection this session opened. No error, no failed statement.
excluded_from_promotion.perf-*.data: raw perf sample files (1.2-2.5 GB each, 4.6 GB total). The derived profile-*-flat.txt / profile-*-callgraph.txt reports and the perf-stat-*.txt counters are promoted and hashed, and every profile number in the report is read from those. The .data files themselves are dispensable work and were DELETED at query completion together with the rest of work/Q20 (SSOT section 19: 'promote required files to raw and delete dispensable work'). They are reproducible from raw/Q20/profile_driver.sh against the pinned binaries.

notes: HEADLINE RE-MEASUREMENT. The first three CUBRID blocks passed the WARM gate's LEVEL test (40 consecutive self-repeats held 3.146-3.205 s, half-split trend -0.1576%) but failed the physical-read half of the SSOT section 12 WARM proof: the trace of an equally converged statement reported ioread: 204665. The headline was re-measured under a proven-resident pool (1.992000 s, /proc read_bytes delta EXACTLY 0 on all three blocks, trace ioread: 0). The superseded blocks are RETAINED as Q20-cubrid-lowresident-* and are valid measurements of a real engine state, used as such in report section 5; they are simply not the section 12 headline.

COLD-POOL A/B. cub_server was restarted ONCE through the mandated wrapper (cubrid-server-ctl.sh restart), AFTER every headline, telemetry and perf artifact had been captured, to run the residency A/B. cub_server pid changes 1612732 -> 2646189; the post-restart ownership gate re-resolved the same executable and SHA-256, cpuset was reapplied to all 124 TIDs (0 off-cpuset) and parallelism/data_buffer_size were re-verified. No headline value was measured after the restart. The A/B independently reproduces the headline level (phase A statements 2-30: 1.916-2.043 s).

The A/B FALSIFIED the hypothesis it was built to test. It was designed to confirm IMP-018 (a session's pages escape to the shared pool only when a DIFFERENT session touches them). From a cold pool Q20 instead reaches full residency within ONE statement and holds it for 30, and the foreign touch changes nothing. The retained finding is IMP-002's history-dependent equilibrium: the working set is 490,005 pages = 93.5% of the 524,288-page pool, so it fits from cold but cannot reclaim space from a pre-existing foreign working set, costing 1.5874x with plan, query text and page fetch count (1,300,830) constant.

cubrid statdump buffer counters again read delta 0 over a whole block on this server (Q14/Q16/Q18/Q19 defect, reconfirmed on a 12.8 s block and again on a settled single-statement probe where even Num_data_page_fetches read 0). Retained in the headline JSONs but EXCLUDED from every calculation; CUBRID buffer/IO evidence rests on /proc read_bytes+syscr and the engine trace instead.

TAG COLLISION, repaired by re-measurement not reconstruction. The first block-regime telemetry pass tagged BOTH PostgreSQL configurations 'headline', so telemetry_run.py wrote both to Q20-postgresql-headline-telemetry.json and the derived pass overwrote the native one before it was renamed. The native block telemetry was RE-RUN under the distinct tag 'nativeblock' (Q20-postgresql-nativeblock-*); the card reads that artifact. Nothing was recovered from a log line.

Two single-statement telemetry runs (Q20-*-telemetry.json, without '-headline-') are retained but are NOT card inputs: on PostgreSQL a single statement in a fresh connection IS the burn-in statement (1.6228 s against a 1.0963 s plateau on the derived variant), so those runs measure the burn-in. The block-regime runs supersede them. CUBRID has no burn-in on Q20 and its two figures agree, which is the cross-check that the block-regime instrument is the right one.

Both sides of the CONTROLLED PAIR (CUBRID native, PostgreSQL derived) are zero-physical-read, so no I/O residency leaks into F_units or F_cpu. PostgreSQL NATIVE cannot reach zero by construction (589,094 pages per statement) and that is confined to F_plan, where it belongs.
